 Present
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anil Kumar Choudhary
By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2. This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a prayer to quash and set aside the order dated 22.07.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 passed by Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ramgarh in connection with F.I.R. of Mandu (Kujju O.P.) P.S. Case No.192 of 2017 registered for the offences punishable under Section 420, 409, 468, 467, 471 of the Indian Penal Code which is pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramgarh.

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ramgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The brief facts of the case is that the petitioner has allegedly misappropriated Rs.17,01,000/- and against the said misappropriation, the petitioner has deposited Rs.21,00,000/- with interest and the petitioner who was under suspension has been reinstated after revoking the suspension.

After Ashok Kumar Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand ... Opposite ... on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92686611/
1 reinstatement the petitioner served the department between the period 2015-2018 but all of a sudden on 05.08.2017, F.I.R. was lodged and the petitioner came to know about the said F.I.R. on 05.05.2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner was arrested in connection with the said case and was dismissed from the service.
The petitioner who is an accused person of the said case, filed a petition for discharge in the court of learned A.C.J.M., Ramgarh in G.R. Case No.844 of 2017.

The learned A.C.J.M.,
Ramgarh considered the allegation against the petitioner that while the petitioner was serving as Special Post Master at Kuju Sub Post Office from 17.05.2010 to 17.06.2013 had received depositors transfer application of MIS Account but after transfer of the account to the transferee post office the petitioner did not close the account on the MIS ledger and in criminal conspiracy with the co- accused persons withdrew Government money in closed MIS account of Kuju S.O. whose accounts were already transferred to transferee post office by putting false and fictitious signature in withdrawal form of the respective account and has thus, misappropriated Government money to the tune of Rs.17,01,000/-.

As the learned A.C.J.M., Ramgarh from perusal of the F.I.R. found that there is allegation against the petitioner of having fraudulently withdrawn the said amount and after considering the materials available in the case diary, rejected the petition for discharge vide his order dated 06.01.2022.

In Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 the learned Sessions Judge, Ramgarh considered that there was sufficient material to show that prima facie the petitioner has committed the offences alleged and it cannot be said that the allegations against the petitioner are groundless and only because the defalcated amount has been recovered from the petitioner that will not exonerate him from the criminal liability and dismissed the criminal revision.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent.
The F.I.R. has been registered after inordinate delay of five years and the order of Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 passed by the Sessions Judge, Ramgarh, has been passed in a mechanical manner.
It is next submitted that the petitioner has been granted regular bail.

Hence, it is submitted that the order dated 22.07.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 passed by Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ramgarh in connection with F.I.R. of Mandu (Kujju O.P.) P.S. Case No.192 of 2017 which is pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramgarh, be quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ramgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
5. Learned Addl.P.P. appearing for the State vehemently opposes the prayer to quash and set aside the order dated 22.07.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 by the Sessions Judge,
Ramgarh in connection with F.I.R. of Mandu (Kujju O.P.) P.S. Case No.192 of 2017 which is pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramgarh.

Learned Addl.P.P. next submits that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner of having committed the offences punishable under Sections 467, 468 as well as Section 409 of the Indian Penal Code and other offences.

Hence, it is submitted that there is no illegality in the order dated 22.07.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 by the Sessions Judge, Ramgarh in connection with F.I.R. of Mandu (Kujju O.P.) P.S. Case No.192 of 2017 which is pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramgarh.
It is lastly submitted that this Cr.

M.P., being without any merit,
be dismissed.

6. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record; it is pertinent to mention here that it is a settled principle of law Ashok Kumar Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Opposite ... on 19 August, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92686611/
2 that where material placed before the court discloses grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained, the court will be fully justified in framing the charge.
If on the basis of the materials on record the court would form prima facie opinion that the accused might have committed offence it can frame the charge.

At the time of framing charges, the probative value of the material on record has to be drawn into and the court is not expected to go deep into the matter and hold that the material would not warrant conviction.

The court is required to evaluate the material in the record at this stage only with a view to find out if the facts emerging therefrom taken at the face value discloses the existences of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence and it is trite that at the stage of consideration of an application for discharge, the court has to proceed with the presumption that the materials brought on record by the prosecution are proved and evaluate such materials with a view to find out whether the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value disclose existence of the ingredients of the offence, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of State by the Inspector of Police, Chennai vs. S. Selvi reported in 2018 AIR SC 81.
7.

Now, coming to the facts of the case; there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner of misappropriating Government money to the tune of Rs.17,01,000/- by committing forgery for the purpose of cheating and having used forged documents as genuine also for cheating.

Hence, this Court is of the considered view that there is no illegality in the order dated 22.07.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 passed by the Sessions Judge, Ramgarh in connection with F.I.R.
of Mandu (Kujju O.P.) P.S. Case No.192 of 2017 which is pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramgarh.

8. Accordingly, the prayer to quash the order dated 22.07.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2022 by the Sessions Judge, Ramgarh in connection with F.I.R. of Mandu (Kujju O.P.) P.S. Case No.192 of 2017 which is pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Ramgarh is rejected.
9. In the result, this Cr.M.P. is dismissed.
